steps.title: Set the container
steps.body: Make it feel like a date: snacks, tea, wine, a walk, dessert first.

steps.title: Ask three questions
steps.body: “What feels financially stressful right now?” “Where do you need more clarity or autonomy?” “What feels fair to both of us?” Start with a soft and curious tone.

steps.title: End with one small decision
steps.body: Agree one small decision before you stop.

steps.title: Do it monthly
steps.body: Keep it short, and plan the next one for a month from now.

body.intro: Phones in a stack. First to look picks up the tab.

steps.title: Stack them
steps.body: Both phones face down in the middle of the table.

steps.title: Eat
steps.body: Dinner without devices.

steps.title: First to look pays
steps.body: Whoever is first to look at their phone picks up the tab. At home, they do the dishes.

body.intro: One hour each to recharge, guilt free.

steps.title: Agree how much
steps.body: Agree how much “me time” each of you needs to recharge without feeling neglected.

steps.title: Take your hour
steps.body: A quiet hour with a book, a solo walk, or something you care about.

steps.title: Keep it even
steps.body: You both get the same amount. Respecting the boundary is the point.

body.intro: Fifteen minutes each to unload the day. Not about each other.

steps.title: Pick a time
steps.body: Same time each day, like 7 pm or before bed.

steps.title: Take turns
steps.body: Each of you gets fifteen minutes to talk about stress outside the relationship.

steps.title: Listening rules
steps.body: Don’t give unsolicited advice: understanding must precede advice. Stay focused on your partner, take their side and show it’s you two against the problem.

steps.title: Close with affection
steps.body: Say what you understood, validate how they feel, and end with a hug.

body.intro: A new healthy recipe, planned and cooked together.

steps.title: Plan the menu
steps.body: One of you picks a new recipe and checks what’s already at home.

steps.title: Shop
steps.body: Get what’s missing. Under $25 for two.

steps.title: Cook it together
steps.body: Split the jobs and cook the new recipe together.

steps.title: Eat together
steps.body: Phones away. Would you make it again?

body.intro: Agree the holidays before the family calls do.

steps.title: Name what’s hard
steps.body: Talk through the things you’re not comfortable with at family gatherings.

steps.title: Same page
steps.body: Agree how you’ll support each other while you’re there.

steps.title: Set expectations
steps.body: Keep them realistic: who you’ll see, when and for how long.

steps.title: Save it
steps.body: Add the dates to Plans so you both see them.

body.intro: One item from your bucket lists, on the calendar.

steps.title: Start from your matches
steps.body: Look at the Bucket List picks you both chose.

steps.title: Imagine it
steps.body: Ask: “What’s a one-day adventure you could imagine us having together?” and “Which of the things your partner finds fun are you willing to try?”

steps.title: Plan it
steps.body: Pick one, choose a date and add it to Plans.

steps.title: Save for the big ones
steps.body: For a bigger dream, work together to make it happen: set a savings goal.

body.intro: An hour on your partner’s dream, and how you can back it.

steps.title: Ask about it
steps.body: Start with “What’s the story behind that?” Then ask questions about the dream.

steps.title: Offer support
steps.body: Offer empathy, emotional support and validation.

steps.title: Take part
steps.body: Read about it, help make plans, offer advice if it’s wanted.

steps.title: Offer something real
steps.body: Child-care, transportation, whatever you feel able to offer. Or join the dream on a trial basis.

body.intro: Spend a day giving back to your community or supporting a cause close to your hearts.

steps.title: Pick a cause
steps.body: Volunteer at your local animal shelter, join a charity event, or join a run for a cause.

steps.title: Go together
steps.body: You’re helping, spending time together and staying active.
